_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Papua New Guinea covering ancient settlement (~50,000 years, among earliest outside Africa), Kuk Swamp agriculture (earliest in world ~7000 BCE, UNESCO), extreme linguistic diversity (840+ languages, most linguistically diverse place on Earth), European contact (Portuguese 1512, Dutch, British/German partition), colonial period (British New Guinea/Papua + German New Guinea), WWII (Kokoda Track, Battle of the Coral Sea, Rabaul), Australian trusteeship (1945-1975), independence 1975, Bougainville civil war 1988-98, resource extraction (Ok Tedi, LNG), 2019 Bougainville referendum.

other_languages: 840+ indigenous languages (most linguistically diverse place on Earth)

religion.note: Evangelical Lutheran (largest single, ~19%, German missionaries); Catholic (highlands/coast); United Church (Methodist/London Missionary Society merger); Seventh-day Adventist (~10%); Pentecostal/charismatic growing rapidly; traditional beliefs persist strongly alongside Christianity (syncretism, sorcery beliefs, sanguma accusations leading to violence); cargo cults (John Frum-type, belief in spiritual means to obtain Western goods)

ethnic_groups.name: Papuan
ethnic_groups.notes: Non-Austronesian peoples; inhabit highlands and interior; arrived ~50,000 years ago; extraordinary diversity (hundreds of distinct ethnolinguistic groups: Huli, Enga, Chimbu, Eastern Highlands groups); Highlands first contacted by outside world only in 1930s ('First Contact', shell/steel era, documented in films); wantok system (one-talk, kinship/linguistic affiliation, mutual obligation, corruption driver); payback/tribal warfare (inter-clan violence ongoing, 2024 Enga Province massacre 64+ dead); sing-sing (cultural festivals, elaborate body decoration, bird of paradise plumes); kina shell (traditional currency, gave name to national currency); taro/sweet potato agriculture

ethnic_groups.name: Melanesian (Austronesian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Coastal and island peoples; Austronesian languages; maritime culture; Sepik River art (world-renowned, spirit houses/haus tambaran, masks, carvings); Trobriand Islands (Malinowski's ethnography, kula ring exchange, yam festivals); Bismarck Archipelago; Tolai (Rabaul, shell money/tambu, economically active); Motu (Port Moresby area, hiri trading voyages with lagatoi canoes)

ethnic_groups.name: Bougainvillean
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethnically closer to Solomon Islands (Melanesian, darker skin); Bougainville civil war 1988-98 (Panguna copper mine environmental destruction, BRA independence movement, 15-20k dead, blockade, crisis, peace 2001); 2019 independence referendum (97.7% voted for independence, negotiations ongoing with PNG government, independence not yet implemented); autonomous region since 2005

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Chinese (~20k, business community, periodic anti-Chinese sentiment/riots); Australian (~10k, business/NGO); Filipino; Indian; European; mixed race; uncontacted tribes (interior highlands, estimated small groups never contacted by outside world)

independence.from: Australia (UN trusteeship; peaceful, Michael Somare first PM)

country_profile.notes_unique: Most linguistically diverse place on Earth (840+ living languages, 12% of world's languages in 0.4% of world's area, Tok Pisin lingua franca, no single language spoken by majority, extreme terrain isolates valleys/communities); Kuk Swamp (UNESCO, Western Highlands, earliest independent invention of agriculture ~7000-6500 BCE, taro/banana/yam, predates Mesopotamia, challenges Fertile Crescent primacy); Kokoda Track (WWII, 1942, Australian/PNG soldiers vs Japanese, 96km mountain trail, 625 Australians killed, halted Japanese advance toward Port Moresby, ANZAC mythology, pilgrimage trail today); Bougainville (Panguna copper mine 1972-89, one of world's largest, BHP/Rio Tinto, environmental devastation, Bougainville Revolutionary Army 1988, civil war 15-20k dead, 1997 Sandline Affair mercenary crisis, 2001 peace, 2019 referendum 97.7% independence, negotiations stalled); tribal warfare (payback killings, inter-clan violence, highlands gun violence escalating 2020s, 2024 Enga massacre, state capacity limited, customary law vs state law); sorcery-related violence (sanguma, belief widespread, women accused tortured/burned alive, Sorcery National Action Plan, repeal of Sorcery Act 2013 but killings continue); Ok Tedi mine (environmental disaster, tailings dumped in Fly River, BHP abandoned, compensation); PNG LNG (ExxonMobil, $19B project, 2014-present, resource revenue, 'resource curse' debate, limited benefit to population); bird of paradise (national symbol, flag, elaborate plumage, 38 species, sing-sing headdresses); Highlands Show (Mount Hagen, cultural festival, thousands of warriors in traditional dress); cannibalism (historically practiced, last documented mid-20th century, Michael Rockefeller 1961 disappearance Asmat coast); Sepik River art (masks, carvings, initiation scarification, world museum collections); wantok system (mutual aid network, also source of corruption/nepotism); Port Moresby (consistently ranked most dangerous city in world, raskol gangs); gender-based violence (estimated 70% of women experience, 'man's country'); 85% rural (subsistence agriculture, most people grow own food)

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global. 'rank' = 1 is best/largest.

current_leader.name: James Marape
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Pangu Pati; 'Take Back PNG' (resource nationalism, wants more revenue from mines/LNG); re-elected 2022; Bougainville negotiations (stalling independence implementation); Enga Province violence; corruption concerns; balancing Chinese investment vs traditional Western (Australia/US) alliance; climate/disaster management (Mulitaka landslide 2024)

head_of_state.name: King Charles III
head_of_state.title: King of Papua New Guinea
head_of_state.notes: Constitutional monarch; represented by Governor-General Bob Dadae (since 2017); one of 14 Commonwealth realms; republic periodically discussed but not imminent

former_leaders.name: Peter O'Neill
former_leaders.notes: PNC; 8 years; PNG LNG period; infrastructure spending; arrest warrant issued for fraud (2014, ignored it while PM, constitutional crisis); Bougainville referendum agreement; authoritarian tendencies; resigned 2019 amid party revolt; charged 2020

former_leaders.name: Sir Michael Somare
former_leaders.notes: 'Father of the Nation'; first PM at independence 1975; three terms; Pangu Pati founder; led independence negotiations; longest cumulative PM tenure; ousted 2011 while in hospital (constitutional crisis, O'Neill replaced him while medically incapacitated); died 2021; national hero; nation-builder but also presided over corruption

former_leaders.name: Sir Julius Chan
former_leaders.notes: PPP; Sandline Affair 1997 (hired South African mercenaries to fight Bougainville, military commander Jerry Singirok mutinied, constitutional crisis, Chan forced to resign, scandalized internationally); businessman; Chinese-PNG heritage

former_leaders.name: Paias Wingti
former_leaders.notes: PDM; Highlands politician; economic reforms; forestry controversies; politically resilient
